# opencode-auto-nudge

An [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) plugin that keeps agent sessions alive: it retries failed or empty model turns automatically, gives up loudly instead of silently, and plays distinct sounds when your attention is actually needed — so you stop typing `continue` every few minutes.

## The problem

During long agentic runs, OpenCode sessions can stall in ways that are easy to miss:

- **Provider hiccups** (429 rate limits, 5xx, timeouts) exhaust OpenCode's built-in retries and the turn just ends.
- **Empty responses** — the model returns a turn with zero content (only internal step markers), the loop exits, and nothing tells you.
- **Permission prompts** sit unanswered while you're in another window.

`opencode-auto-nudge` watches session events and closes each of these gaps: transient failures get retried with backoff, empty turns get a "continue exactly where you left off" nudge, and every terminal outcome is surfaced via toast, log line, and sound.

## What it does

| Situation | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Retryable provider error (`429`, `5xx`, timeout, overloaded, network…) | Re-prompts the same session after exponential backoff (3s → 30s), up to `MAX_ATTEMPTS` |
| Turn completed but produced no output | Watchdog detects it on `session.idle` and injects a continuation prompt within seconds |
| Retries exhausted | Explicit "giving up" warn log + error toast + error sound. Never silently stops |
| Permission / question waiting for you | Attention ping, repeated on an interval until you answer |
| Task finished legitimately | Short ascending chime (long turns only) |
| You aborted (`esc`) or typed a message | Nothing is auto-continued; counters reset |

## Sound signals

Sounds are synthesized at startup into `~/.cache/opencode/sounds/` — no asset files needed and no dependency on any specific sound driver or device.

Playback is a **fallback chain**, not a single player: every detected player among `paplay` (PulseAudio), `pw-play` (PipeWire), `ffplay`, `afplay` (macOS), `aplay` (ALSA) is tried in order until one exits successfully. Player detection uses Bun's native `which` inside OpenCode (no shell quirks) with a portable fallback elsewhere. If no player exists at all, the plugin degrades silently to toasts/logs — or, with `AUTO_SOUND_BEL=1`, emits a terminal bell (`\a`) as a last resort (terminal-dependent; many terminals mute it by default).

Each turn-end writes a breadcrumb to `~/.cache/opencode/sounds/debug.json` recording the classification decision (`success`, `skip-short-turn`, `nudged`, …) plus the last playback attempt result — so "why no sound?" is always answerable from one file.

| File | Pattern | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `success.wav` | two ascending tones (880→1318 Hz) | turn completed with real output |
| `error.wav` | descending low buzz (330→196 Hz) | turn died in a non-abort error, or retries were exhausted |
| `attention.wav` | urgent double high ping (1568 Hz) | permission/question needs your decision; re-pings every `AUTO_SOUND_REMIND_MS` up to `AUTO_SOUND_REMIND_MAX` times |

**Deliberate silences** so this doesn't get annoying:

- Turns shorter than `AUTO_SOUND_SHORT_TURN_MS` (you're actively chatting anyway)
- Aborts (`esc`) — you did that on purpose
- Subagent (child) sessions — no false "done!" while the parent keeps working
- Intermediate retry attempts — only outcomes beep
- Headless environments without an audio player — falls back to toasts/logs only

## Installation

Requires [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai). Restart OpenCode after any install method — plugins load once at startup.

**Option A — npm package** (recommended):

```jsonc
// ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugin": ["opencode-auto-nudge"]
}
```

**No sound files to download or install** — the three tones are synthesized programmatically on your machine at every startup (pure JS, ~47 KB of PCM). Nothing ships as binary assets, nothing depends on a particular sound driver.

**Option B — global drop-in** (no npm):

```bash
curl -o ~/.config/opencode/plugins/auto-nudge.ts \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ay8-dev/opencode-auto-nudge/main/index.ts
```

**Option C — per-project drop-in**:

```bash
cp index.ts .opencode/plugins/auto-nudge.ts
```

## Configuration

All knobs are environment variables (set them where you launch `opencode`). Defaults are tuned for unattended runs; everything works out of the box.

### Retry ladder

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `AUTO_NUDGE_MAX_ATTEMPTS` | `5` | Max nudges per failure episode |
| `AUTO_NUDGE_EMPTY_DELAY_MS` | `1500` | Delay before re-prompting an empty response |
| `AUTO_NUDGE_ERROR_BASE_MS` | `3000` | Base delay for error backoff (doubles per attempt) |
| `AUTO_NUDGE_ERROR_MAX_MS` | `30000` | Backoff ceiling |
| `AUTO_NUDGE_MIN_GAP_MS` | `1200` | Collapse duplicate triggers for the same failure |
| `AUTO_NUDGE_BUSY_RECHECK_MS` | `2000` | Wait before re-checking if the session was busy at fire time |
| `AUTO_NUDGE_BUSY_RECHECK_MAX` | `10` | Max busy-rechecks before dropping a retry (logged loudly) |
| `AUTO_NUDGE_TTL_MS` | `300000` | Failure counter expires after this much quiet time |

### Sounds

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `AUTO_SOUND_DISABLE` | unset (`1` disables) | Turn all sounds off; toasts/logs remain |
| `AUTO_SOUND_DIR` | `~/.cache/opencode/sounds` | Where generated wavs live |
| `AUTO_SOUND_SHORT_TURN_MS` | `4000` | Turns faster than this don't play success (interactive chat) |
| `AUTO_SOUND_REMIND_MS` | `20000` | Interval for permission reminders |
| `AUTO_SOUND_REMIND_MAX` | `2` | Extra reminder pings per permission ask |
| `AUTO_SOUND_GAIN` | `100` | Playback gain in percent (20–400) |
| `AUTO_SOUND_BEL` | `0` | Emit terminal bell as last-resort fallback when no player works |

## Safety design

This plugin is built to never make things worse:

- **Hard caps everywhere** — attempt caps, TTL expiry, min-gap deduplication, and bounded rescheduling mean no runaway loops, even if a provider returns instant failures forever.
- **Aborts are sacred** — turns ended by user abort are never auto-continued.
- **User intervention wins** — typing any message resets the failure counters.
- **Failed prompt calls refund their attempt** — a rejected nudge doesn't burn budget.
- **Errors attached to a turn** (auth failures etc.) are not retried — nudging can't fix a bad API key.
- **Every action is logged** under the `[auto-nudge]` tag with service name `auto-nudge`.

## Observability

```bash
grep "\[auto-nudge\]" ~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log
```

Expect lines like:

```
[auto-nudge] session ses_xxx retry 2/5 in 3000ms (empty response)
[auto-nudge] session ses_xxx recovered after 2 nudge(s)
[auto-nudge] giving up on session ses_xxx after 5 attempts (empty response)
[auto-nudge] permission ask detected (per_xxx)
[auto-nudge] sounds on via pw-play
```

Toasts appear in the TUI: warning variants for retries, error variant on give-up.

## Known limitations

- **Same-model retries only.** If a provider is down for good, the ladder burns its attempts and reports loudly. It intentionally does *not* switch models — pair it with a model-failover plugin if you want that layer (mind the overlap: both react to the same events).
- **Heuristic empty detection.** A turn counts as empty when the last assistant message has no text/tool/reasoning parts. Exotic part types could be misclassified.
- **Coupled to OpenCode event shapes** — `session.error`, `session.idle`, `session.status`, `message.updated`, `permission.asked/replied`, `question.asked/replied/rejected` — verified against OpenCode source and live logs (Aug 2026). Both legacy bus names and internal `.v2.` schema names are handled for permissions and questions. Note: the plugin-facing event bus delivers the non-prefixed names; `permission.v2.*` / `question.v2.*` exist only in core internals. Verified against OpenCode 1.18.x; future releases may change shapes and require plugin updates. The `init.json` marker written into `AUTO_SOUND_DIR` at startup (`{"player": "...", "at": "..."}`) doubles as a load-health check: no file = plugin didn't initialize, `"player": null` = no audio player found.
- **Permission reminder depends on `permission.asked`/`permission.replied` events** matching expected id fields; if those change, pings may not repeat (the initial ping comes from the same handler).
- **Subagent sessions are nudged but silent.** A parent that already given up on a child can see up to `MAX_ATTEMPTS` late child-resurrections — usually desirable, occasionally surprising.
- **Tested on Linux (Wayland/PipeWire) with Node/Bun.** macOS/Windows player probing includes `afplay`/`ffplay` paths but is not battle-tested.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Check |
|---|---|
| No sounds at all | Read `~/.cache/opencode/sounds/init.json`: `"players": []` means no player binary was found on PATH. Test manually: `pw-play ~/.cache/opencode/sounds/success.wav` |
| Chime missing on some turns | Read `debug.json`: the last turn's `action` field explains the decision (`skip-short-turn` = under threshold, `skip-child` = subagent, etc.) |
| No sound on a permission prompt but logs show `permission ask detected` | Audio server issue, not the plugin |
| Nudges seem absent | Is there any `[auto-nudge]` line at all? None = plugin didn't load — restart OpenCode |
| Gives up too early/late | Tune `AUTO_NUDGE_MAX_ATTEMPTS` and backoff vars |
| Want silence | `AUTO_SOUND_DISABLE=1` |

## Development

```bash
npm install
npm test        # builds dist/ then runs the offline test suite (no OpenCode instance needed)
```

The test suite mocks the OpenCode SDK client and shell, so it verifies decision logic end-to-end — retry chains, dedup, caps, re-arm, sound routing — without touching a running instance.
